<!-- source: docs/components/DSListCell.md -->

# DSListCell

A consistent list row with leading and trailing slots, an optional tap action, a section header and a hairline divider.

![DSListCell](../media/DSListCell.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSList.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSList.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ListDemo: View {
    @State private var selected = "None yet"

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
                DSSectionHeader("Account", action: "Edit") { selected = "Edit" }

                DSCard(padding: 0) {
                    VStack(spacing: 0) {
                        DSListCell(
                            title: "Ada Lovelace",
                            subtitle: "ada@example.com",
                            leading: { DSAvatar(name: "Ada Lovelace") },
                            action: { selected = "Profile" }
                        )
                        DSDivider(inset: DSSpacing.screenHorizontal)
                        DSListCell(
                            title: "Notifications",
                            trailing: { DSCountBadge(count: 3) },
                            action: { selected = "Notifications" }
                        )
                        DSDivider(inset: DSSpacing.screenHorizontal)
                        DSListCell(title: "Version", subtitle: "0.2.0")
                    }
                }
                .padding(.horizontal, DSSpacing.screenHorizontal)

                Text("Last tapped: \(selected)")
                    .ds(.caption1)
                    .padding(DSSpacing.screenHorizontal)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Wrap groups of cells in a `DSCard(padding: 0)` for the glass look. Cells add their own horizontal padding (`DSSpacing.screenHorizontal`), so use `padding: 0` on the card.

## Parameters

### DSListCell

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `String` | required | Primary text (`.body`). |
| `subtitle` | `String?` | `nil` | Secondary text (`.callout`, secondary color). |
| `leading` | `@ViewBuilder () -> Leading` | `{ EmptyView() }` | View before the text, such as an icon or `DSAvatar`. |
| `trailing` | `@ViewBuilder () -> Trailing` | `{ EmptyView() }` | View after the text, such as a `DSCountBadge`. |
| `action` | `(() -> Void)?` | `nil` | When set, the cell is a button with a chevron. |

### DSSectionHeader

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_ title` | `String` | required | Uppercase overline title. |
| `action` | `String?` | `nil` | Label of the trailing text button. |
| `onAction` | `(() -> Void)?` | `nil` | Called when the button is tapped. The button only appears when both `action` and `onAction` are set. |

### DSDivider

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inset` | `CGFloat` | `0` | Leading inset, so the line can start under the text instead of under the icon. |

## Variants

- **Static row**: omit `action` and the cell is plain content without chevron.
- **Tappable row**: pass `action` and the whole row (padding included) becomes the tap target, with a trailing chevron and a `.light` haptic.
- **Divider**: a 1pt `palette.divider` line; it is the only separator, there are no borders.

## Behavior

- Tappable cells use a plain button style: no system highlight, no press animation. Wrap them in `DSInteractiveCard` if you want a scale-on-press card instead.
- The header action fires a `.light` haptic as well.

## Accessibility

- A tappable cell is a `Button`: VoiceOver reads the title, subtitle and any text in the slots as one label, and activating it calls `action`. A static cell is a plain stack whose pieces are read in order.
- The chevron is a decorative SF Symbol; the section header title is read as a normal text element.
- Override with `.accessibilityLabel("…")` or `.accessibilityHint("…")` on the cell.
- Text uses `.ds(_:)` styles, so rows grow with Dynamic Type.

## See also

- [DSCard](DSCard.md) for grouping rows
- [DSAvatar](DSAvatar.md) and [DSBadge](DSBadge.md) for slots
- [DSEmptyState](DSEmptyState.md) for an empty list
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSCarousel.md -->

# DSCarousel

A snapping carousel where the neighbouring items peek in at the edges and lean away with a little depth. The page index is a plain `Int`, so it pairs directly with `DSPageControl`.

![DSCarousel](../media/DSCarousel.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSCarousel.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSCarousel.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct Trip: Identifiable {
    let id: Int
    let city: String
    let price: String
}

struct CarouselDemo: View {
    @State private var page = 0
    private let trips = [
        Trip(id: 0, city: "Lisbon", price: "$480"),
        Trip(id: 1, city: "Kyoto", price: "$1,240"),
        Trip(id: 2, city: "Oaxaca", price: "$620")
    ]

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                DSCarousel(trips, currentPage: $page) { trip in
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                        Text(trip.city).ds(.title2)
                        Text(trip.price).ds(.callout)
                    }
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .bottomLeading)
                    .padding(DSSpacing.md)
                    .dsSurface(.glass, radius: DSRadius.card)
                }
                .frame(height: 200)

                DSPageControl(currentPage: $page, numberOfPages: trips.count)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `RandomAccessCollection` of `Identifiable` | required | The items. Each element's `id` identifies its page. |
| `currentPage` | `Binding<Int>` | none | The page index. Scrolling updates it; changing it scrolls there with a spring. Out-of-range values are clamped. Leave it out and the carousel keeps its own index. |
| `peek` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xxxl` | Margin on each side of the centred item. `peek - spacing` of each neighbour shows. |
| `spacing` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.sm` | Gap between items. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle?` | `.selection` | Fired once per page change. `nil` for none. |
| `content` | `(Element) -> View` | required | The view for one item. Trailing closure. |

Each item is as wide as the carousel minus `peek` on both sides. Give the carousel a height and let each item fill it with `.frame(maxHeight: .infinity)`: content taller than the carousel is clipped.

## Variants

```swift
struct CarouselCompactDemo: View {
    private let tags = [
        Trip(id: 0, city: "Lisbon", price: "$480"),
        Trip(id: 1, city: "Kyoto", price: "$1,240")
    ]

    var body: some View {
        DSCarousel(tags, peek: DSSpacing.lg, spacing: DSSpacing.sm, haptic: nil) { trip in
            Text(trip.city)
                .ds(.title3)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 72)
                .dsSurface(.glassThin, radius: DSRadius.surface)
        }
        .frame(height: 80)
    }
}
```
Smaller peek and spacing, no haptic. Without `currentPage` the carousel manages its own index.

## Behavior

- Scrolling snaps to whole items.
- Items away from the centre shrink to about 90%, fade to about 60% and yaw a few degrees towards the centre.
- Setting `currentPage` from code scrolls there with `DSAnimation.springSmooth` (without animation under Reduce Motion). Only user scrolling fires the haptic.
- Reduce Motion: the scale, fade and yaw are skipped (items stay at full size). Snapping stays.

## Accessibility

- The carousel is a container labelled "Carousel" whose value reads "Page 2 of 5". Items stay individually accessible.
- Give each item its own accessibility label inside `content`.

## See also

- [DSPageControl](DSPageControl.md)
- [DSCard](DSCard.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSSheet.md -->

# DSSheet

A Velvet-styled native sheet: detents, a visible grabber, a glass background, and your theme carried into the content.

![DSSheet](../media/DSSheet.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSSheet.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSSheet.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct SheetDemo: View {
    @State private var showShare = false

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            DSButton("Share trip", icon: "square.and.arrow.up") { showShare = true }
                .dsScreenPadding()
        }
        .dsSheet(isPresented: $showShare) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                Text("Share trip").ds(.title2)
                DSListCell(title: "Copy link", leading: { Image(systemName: "link") })
                DSListCell(title: "Message", leading: { Image(systemName: "message") })
            }
            .padding(DSSpacing.xl)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isPresented` | `Binding<Bool>` | required | Whether the sheet is showing. |
| `item` | `Binding<Item?>` | required | The item-driven overload: the sheet shows while non-nil. `Item` is `Identifiable`. |
| `detents` | `Set<PresentationDetent>` | `[.medium, .large]` | Heights the sheet can rest at. |
| `onDismiss` | `(() -> Void)?` | `nil` | Called after dismissal. |
| `content` | `() -> Content` (or `(Item) -> Content`) | required | The sheet body. |

## When to use it

Use `dsSheet` instead of plain `.sheet` when you want the Velvet look without repeating the modifiers: it sets the detents and the visible grabber, picks a glass background, and passes the theme into the sheet (a sheet is a separate view tree, so your presenter's theme would otherwise reset to the default). Keep plain `.sheet` when you need a fully custom background or presentation.

## Variants

Small confirmation sheet with a fixed height:

```swift
.dsSheet(isPresented: $confirming, detents: [.height(220)]) {
    VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
        Text("Delete this trip?").ds(.title3)
        DSButton("Delete", variant: .destructive, isFullWidth: true) { confirming = false }
    }
    .padding(DSSpacing.xl)
}
```

Maps-style persistent sheet: the content behind stays interactive while the sheet is at its smaller detent.

```swift
.dsSheet(isPresented: $showPlaces, detents: [.height(160), .medium, .large]) {
    PlacesList()
        .presentationBackgroundInteraction(.enabled(upThrough: .medium))
        .interactiveDismissDisabled()
}
```

Item-driven: the sheet shows while the item is non-nil.

```swift
.dsSheet(item: $selectedTrip) { trip in
    Text(trip.name).ds(.title2).padding(DSSpacing.xl)
}
```

## Behavior

- It is the system sheet: interactive dismissal, scroll hand-off and keyboard handling all come from SwiftUI.
- Applies `.presentationDetents` and a visible drag indicator.
- On iOS 26 and macOS 26 the system background (Liquid Glass) is left alone. On earlier systems the background is `.regularMaterial`.
- Reduce Transparency: the background is the solid elevated surface color on every system.
- The content gets the presenter's theme and is marked as not on the gradient backdrop.
- No haptic: presenting a sheet is not an action.

## Accessibility

- VoiceOver treats it as a standard sheet; the grabber supports the standard dismiss gesture.
- Give the sheet content its own heading and labelled controls.
- Honors Reduce Transparency.

## See also

- [DSCard](DSCard.md)
- [DSListCell](DSListCell.md)
- [DSToast](DSToast.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSBadge.md -->

# DSBadge

Compact pill labels for status and categories, plus a notification count badge that hides itself at zero and caps at 99+.

![DSBadge](../media/DSBadge.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSBadge.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSBadge.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct BadgeDemo: View {
    @State private var unread = 3

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                    DSBadge("Beta")
                    DSBadge("Pro", variant: .filled)
                    DSBadge("Draft", variant: .outline)
                    DSBadge("Live", color: .green)
                }

                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                    Image(systemName: "bell.fill")
                        .font(.title)
                        .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) {
                            DSCountBadge(count: unread)
                                .offset(x: DSSpacing.xs, y: -DSSpacing.xs)
                        }
                    DSBadge("Mark all read", variant: .soft)
                        .onTapGesture { unread = 0 }
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

### DSBadge

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_ text` | `String` | required | The label (unlabeled first argument). |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Fill for `.filled`, tint for `.soft` and `.outline`. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `variant` | `DSBadgeVariant` | `.soft` | `.filled`, `.soft` or `.outline`. |

### DSCountBadge

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | `Int` | required | Number to show. Renders nothing at 0 or below; shows `99+` above 99. |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Fill color. Defaults to the palette's error color. |

## Variants

| Variant | Default look | With a custom `color` |
|---|---|---|
| `.soft` (default) | Accent at 12% fill, `theme.ink` text | Color at 12% fill, color text |
| `.filled` | Accent fill, `theme.onAccent` text | Color fill, `textOnPrimary` text |
| `.outline` | No fill, 1pt `theme.ink` outline and text | Color outline and text |

`DSCountBadge` is always a filled capsule with `textOnPrimary` text, at least `DSSpacing.lg` square.

## Behavior

- Static components: no motion and no haptics. Pair them with `.dsPopIn()` or `.dsBreathe(.subtle)` (see [Motion](Motion.md)) if you want life.
- `DSCountBadge` removes itself from the layout when `count` is 0, so you can bind it straight to a model value.

## Accessibility

- `DSBadge` and `DSCountBadge` are plain text, so VoiceOver reads the label or the number as shown (`99+` is read as written). Add context from outside, for example `.accessibilityLabel("3 unread notifications")` on the count badge or on the view it decorates.
- Dynamic Type: both badges keep a fixed size for now (fixed-size fonts from the `.buttonSmall` / `.badge` text styles); they do not grow with the user's text size. Keep badge text short.

## See also

- [DSAvatar](DSAvatar.md) for identity
- [DSListCell](DSListCell.md) for badges in trailing slots
- [DSCard](DSCard.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSAvatar.md -->

# DSAvatar

A circular avatar that loads a remote photo and falls back to tinted initials, so it never shows an empty circle.

![DSAvatar](../media/DSAvatar.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSBadge.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSBadge.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct AvatarDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                    DSAvatar(name: "Ada Lovelace")
                    DSAvatar(name: "Grace Hopper", size: 56)
                    DSAvatar(name: "Linus", size: 32)
                }

                DSAvatar(
                    name: "Margaret Hamilton",
                    imageURL: URL(string: "https://example.com/margaret.jpg"),
                    size: 72
                )
                .accessibilityLabel("Margaret Hamilton")
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `String` | required | Full name. Initials come from the first letter of the first and last words. |
| `imageURL` | `URL?` | `nil` | Remote photo, loaded with `AsyncImage`. |
| `size` | `CGFloat` | `40` | Diameter in points. |

## Variants

- **Initials** (no `imageURL`): accent at 15% fill with rounded semibold initials in `theme.ink`, sized at 40% of the avatar.
- **Photo**: the image is scaled to fill and clipped to a circle.
- **Fallback**: while the image loads or if it fails, the initials view is shown instead.
- A one-word name gives one letter (`"Linus"` gives `L`); `"Ada Lovelace"` gives `AL`; middle names are skipped.

## Behavior

- No motion and no haptics. Add `.dsPopIn()` for an entrance or `.dsBreathe()` for a "waiting" avatar (see [Motion](Motion.md)).
- Everything is derived from the theme, so the tint follows the active gradient.

## Accessibility

- The view carries no label of its own: VoiceOver reads the initials text (for example "AL") for the fallback, and nothing useful for a photo. Add `.accessibilityLabel("Ada Lovelace")` from outside, as in the snippet above.
- The initials use a font derived from `size`, so they scale with the avatar, not with Dynamic Type. Choose `size` for the layout you want.

## See also

- [DSListCell](DSListCell.md) (avatar as the leading view)
- [DSBadge](DSBadge.md) (count badge on an avatar)
- [Motion](Motion.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSNumberTicker.md -->

# DSNumberTicker

A number whose digits roll like an odometer. Each digit slides to its new value, staggered from the units digit, while separators and currency symbols stay put.

![DSNumberTicker](../media/DSNumberTicker.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSNumberTicker.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSNumberTicker.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct NumberTickerDemo: View {
    @State private var balance = 1_284.50

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                Text("Balance").ds(.overline)
                DSNumberTicker(balance, format: .currency(code: "USD"))
                DSButton("Add $100") { balance += 100 }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `Double` or `Int` | required | The number to show. The `Int` form is grouped with no decimals. |
| `format` | `FormatStyle` (`Double` to `String`) | required for `Double` | `.number`, `.currency(code:)`, `.percent`, `.number.precision(...)`. Follows the user's locale. |
| `style` | `DSTextStyle` | `.displayMedium` | Use a style with monospaced digits (`.displayLarge`, `.displayMedium`, `.numeric`). |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Text color. Defaults to the theme's primary text color. |

Only ASCII digits (0-9) roll. Anything else the format produces, including other numeral systems, is shown as static text.

## Variants

```swift
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
    DSNumberTicker(8_432, style: .displayLarge)
    DSNumberTicker(0.42, format: .percent, style: .numeric)
    DSNumberTicker(3.14159, format: .number.precision(.fractionLength(2)))
}
```

## Behavior

- Digits roll with a smooth spring, 0.03 s later for each place to the left of the units digit.
- Digits are counted from the right, so going from 99 to 100 keeps the existing digits and fades in the new leading one.
- Each digit's width and height come from the text style, so the number never changes height as it rolls.
- The ticker never compresses: it always takes the width its formatted value needs. Give it room (or pick a smaller `style`) for long currency strings such as "US$ 12,906.40".
- No haptics: it's a display.
- Reduce Motion: digits don't roll. The new value appears with a short crossfade.

## Accessibility

- One element. VoiceOver reads the full formatted value (for example "$1,384.50"), not individual digits.
- Marked as updating frequently, so VoiceOver doesn't announce every change.
- Text scales with Dynamic Type through the DS text styles.

## See also

- [DSStepper](DSStepper.md)
- [DSCard](DSCard.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/Charts.md -->

# Charts

Two light charts with no Swift Charts dependency: `DSSparkline`, a trend line that draws itself and morphs to new data, and `DSBarChart`, bars that grow from the baseline and can be scrubbed to select.

![Charts](../media/Charts.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSCharts.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSCharts.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ChartsDemo: View {
    @State private var revenue: [Double] = [12, 18, 14, 22, 19, 27, 24, 31, 28, 36]
    @State private var week: [Double] = [12, 18, 9, 22, 15, 6, 11]
    @State private var selected: Int?

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                DSCard {
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                        Text("Revenue").ds(.callout)
                        DSSparkline(revenue, accessibilityLabel: "Revenue trend")
                            .frame(height: 72)
                    }
                }

                DSCard {
                    DSBarChart(
                        week,
                        labels: ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"],
                        selection: $selected,
                        accessibilityLabel: "Orders this week"
                    )
                    .frame(height: 180)
                }

                DSButton("Shuffle data", isFullWidth: true) {
                    revenue = revenue.map { _ in Double.random(in: 10...40) }
                    week = week.map { _ in Double.random(in: 2...30) }
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

### DSSparkline

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | `[Double]` | required | The samples, oldest first. Unlabeled first argument. Non-finite values count as 0. |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Line, fill and dot color. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `lineWidth` | `CGFloat` | `2` | Stroke width. |
| `showsFill` | `Bool` | `true` | Fade a gradient of the line color under the line. |
| `showsLastPoint` | `Bool` | `true` | Show the breathing dot on the latest value. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `String` | `"Trend"` | What the chart shows, spoken before the summary. |

### DSBarChart

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | `[Double]` | required | One value per bar. Unlabeled first argument. Negative values clamp to 0. |
| `labels` | `[String]?` | `nil` | Text under each bar, matched by index. |
| `selection` | `Binding<Int?>?` | `nil` | Index of the selected bar. Pass a binding to make the chart interactive. |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Bar color. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `String` | `"Chart"` | What the chart shows. |

Both charts fill the space they are given. Set a height, for example `.frame(height: 72)`.

## Variants

```swift
DSSparkline(revenue, color: DSColors.success, showsFill: false, showsLastPoint: false)
    .frame(height: 40)

DSBarChart(week, color: DSColors.info)
    .frame(height: 96)
```
A sparkline without fill or dot is a plain line, good for table rows. A bar chart without a `selection` binding is static: no gesture, no value label.

## Behavior

- **Scale.** The sparkline maps the lowest value to the bottom of its frame and the highest to the top; flat data is a centred line. The curve is monotone, so it never overshoots the data. The bar chart scales to the tallest bar and starts at zero.
- **Draw-on.** On appear the sparkline line draws itself in one second, the fill fades in behind it, and the dot appears last and breathes.
- **Morph.** When `values` changes and keeps its length, the sparkline line morphs to the new shape and the bars spring to their new heights. A different length redraws the sparkline.
- **Bars.** Bars have rounded tops and grow from the baseline with staggered springs. Negative values clamp to 0.
- **Selection.** Tap a bar, or drag horizontally across the bars, to scrub (vertical drags are left to an enclosing scroll view): each new bar fires a selection haptic and a value label rises above it. Lifting your finger keeps the selection, and tapping the selected bar again clears it. While a bar is selected the others dim.
- Reduce Motion: no draw-on, morph or growth. Data appears at rest, and sparkline changes crossfade. The dot does not breathe.

## Accessibility

- The sparkline is one element: your `accessibilityLabel`, with a spoken summary such as "12 values, from 3 to 18, latest 15".
- Both charts provide an audio graph, so VoiceOver users can play the chart as sound ("Audio Graphs" in the rotor).
- Each bar is its own element ("Mon, 12"). With a `selection` binding each bar is a button that selects it, and the selected bar reports the selected trait.
- Value labels use `.ds(_:)` text, which scales with Dynamic Type.

## See also

- [Progress](Progress.md) for determinate fractions
- [Motion](Motion.md) for `dsBreathe`
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSToast.md -->

# DSToast

A transient, glass-backed message with a status icon for success, error, warning and info.

![DSToast](../media/DSToast.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSToast.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSToast.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

`DSToast` is just the view: you decide when it appears, fire the haptic and dismiss it. This is the usual pattern, an overlay driven by state, with the haptic on presentation and a `.task` that dismisses after a moment:

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ToastDemo: View {
    @State private var toast: (message: String, type: DSToastType)?

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                DSButton("Save", isFullWidth: true) {
                    show("Saved to your library", type: .success)
                }
                DSButton("Simulate failure", variant: .secondary, isFullWidth: true) {
                    show("Couldn't connect", type: .error)
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
        .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
            if let toast {
                DSToast(toast.message, type: toast.type)
                    .padding(.bottom, DSSpacing.md)
                    .transition(.move(edge: .bottom).combined(with: .opacity))
                    .task(id: toast.message) {
                        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.5))
                        withAnimation(DSAnimation.springSmooth) { self.toast = nil }
                    }
            }
        }
    }

    private func show(_ message: String, type: DSToastType) {
        withAnimation(DSAnimation.springSmooth) { toast = (message, type) }
        switch type {
        case .success: DSHapticEngine.shared.fire(.success)
        case .error:   DSHapticEngine.shared.fire(.error)
        case .warning: DSHapticEngine.shared.fire(.warning)
        case .info:    DSHapticEngine.shared.fire(.light)
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_ message` | `String` | required | The message text. |
| `type` | `DSToastType` | `.info` | `.success`, `.error`, `.warning` or `.info`. |

## Variants

| `DSToastType` | Icon | Color | Matching haptic (you fire it) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.success` | `checkmark.circle.fill` | `palette.success` | `.success` |
| `.error` | `xmark.circle.fill` | `palette.error` | `.error` |
| `.warning` | `exclamationmark.triangle.fill` | `palette.warning` | `.warning` |
| `.info` (default) | `info.circle.fill` | `palette.info` | `.light` |

## Behavior

- The toast sits on `.ultraThinMaterial` with a `.lg` shadow, rounded to `DSRadius.md`, and spans the width with the standard screen margin.
- It has no presentation logic: no timer, no animation, no haptic. The snippet shows the caller's side (a spring from `DSAnimation`, `DSHapticEngine.shared.fire(_:)`, and a delayed dismissal). Use the `Examples/VelvetGallery` Toast screen as a reference.
- `DSToastType` has no public haptic mapping; copy the table above (the `switch` in the snippet).
- Under Reduce Motion, swap the slide transition for `.opacity` in your overlay.

## Accessibility

- One element: VoiceOver reads it as "<Type>: <message>" with the types "Success", "Error", "Warning" and "Info" (for example "Success: Saved to your library").
- It is announced when it appears, so users hear it without moving focus. Keep it on screen long enough to be useful, and consider longer timeouts for errors.
- The icon is decorative; the type is spoken as the prefix.
- The text uses `.ds(.callout)`, which scales with Dynamic Type.

## See also

- [DSEmptyState](DSEmptyState.md)
- [Progress](Progress.md) for long-running work
- [DSButton](DSButton.md) as the typical trigger
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSEmptyState.md -->

# DSEmptyState

A centered empty-list or no-results placeholder: a light icon, a title, a short message and an optional call-to-action button.

![DSEmptyState](../media/DSEmptyState.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSToast.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSToast.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct EmptyStateDemo: View {
    @State private var items: [String] = []

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            if items.isEmpty {
                DSEmptyState(
                    icon: "tray",
                    title: "Nothing here yet",
                    message: "Saved recipes show up here so you can find them later.",
                    actionTitle: "Add a recipe"
                ) {
                    items.append("Shakshuka")
                }
            } else {
                VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                    ForEach(items, id: \.self) { item in
                        DSCard { Text(item).ds(.body) }
                    }
                }
                .dsScreenPadding()
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `String` | required | SF Symbol name, drawn at 48pt light weight in the tertiary text color. |
| `title` | `String` | required | Headline (`.title2`). |
| `message` | `String` | required | Supporting text (`.callout`, secondary color, centered). |
| `actionTitle` | `String?` | `nil` | Label of the call-to-action button. |
| `action` | `(() -> Void)?` | `nil` | Button handler. The button only appears when both `actionTitle` and `action` are set. |

## Variants

- **Informational**: omit `actionTitle` and `action` for a read-only state ("No results for 'xyz'").
- **With a call to action**: pass both and a primary `DSButton` appears under the message (it brings its own `.medium` haptic and press scale).

## Behavior

- Static layout: no entrance animation. Add `.dsPopIn()` to the icon or the whole view if you want one (see [Motion](Motion.md)).
- The view pads itself by `DSSpacing.xxl`; center it in its container yourself, for example inside a `DSScreen` or a `frame(maxHeight: .infinity)`.

## Accessibility

- The icon is an SF Symbol without a label; the title and message are read in order, followed by the button. The title is a normal text element rather than a heading, so add `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)` from outside if you want heading navigation.
- The button is a labelled `DSButton`.
- Text uses `.ds(_:)` styles and scales with Dynamic Type; the 48pt icon is fixed.

## See also

- [DSListCell](DSListCell.md) for the populated list
- [DSTypewriterText](DSTypewriterText.md) for a livelier headline
- [DSToast](DSToast.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

# Progress

Progress indicators that animate to their value instead of jumping: ring, bar, gradient bar, step dots, a counting number and a skeleton shimmer.

![Progress](../media/Progress.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSProgressAnimation.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Animation/DSProgressAnimation.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ProgressDemo: View {
    @State private var progress = 0.35
    @State private var step = 2

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                DSCircularProgress(progress: progress, size: 96)
                DSAnimatedNumber(value: progress * 100, style: .displayMedium)
                DSLinearProgress(progress: progress)
                DSGradientProgress(progress: progress)
                DSStepProgress(currentStep: step, totalSteps: 4)

                DSButton("Advance", isFullWidth: true) {
                    progress = min(progress + 0.15, 1)
                    step = min(step + 1, 4)
                }

                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: DSRadius.control, style: .continuous)
                        .fill(Color.gray.opacity(0.25))
                        .frame(height: 16)
                        .dsShimmer()
                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: DSRadius.control, style: .continuous)
                        .fill(Color.gray.opacity(0.25))
                        .frame(width: 160, height: 16)
                        .dsShimmer()
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

### DSCircularProgress

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `progress` | `Double` | required | 0 to 1, clamped. |
| `lineWidth` | `CGFloat` | `6` | Ring thickness. |
| `size` | `CGFloat` | `80` | Diameter. |
| `primaryColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Ring color. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `trackColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Track color. Defaults to the palette border color. |

### DSLinearProgress

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `progress` | `Double` | required | 0 to 1, clamped. |
| `height` | `CGFloat` | `6` | Bar height. |
| `primaryColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Fill color. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `trackColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Track color. Defaults to the palette border color. |

### DSGradientProgress

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `progress` | `Double` | required | 0 to 1, clamped. |
| `height` | `CGFloat` | `8` | Bar height. |
| `colors` | `[Color]?` | `nil` | Gradient stops, left to right. Defaults to the theme gradient's stops. |
| `trackColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Track color. Defaults to the palette border color. |

### DSStepProgress

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `currentStep` | `Int` | required | Number of completed steps (segments filled). |
| `totalSteps` | `Int` | required | Number of segments. |
| `activeColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Completed segments. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `inactiveColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Remaining segments. Defaults to the palette border color. |

### DSAnimatedNumber

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `Double` | required | The number to count to. |
| `format` | `String` | `"%.0f"` | `String(format:)` format, for example `"%.1f"`. |
| `style` | `DSTextStyle` | `.displayLarge` | Text style (monospaced digits). |

### `.dsShimmer()`

`func dsShimmer() -> some View`, no parameters. A soft highlight sweeps across the view in a 1.5s linear loop. It is width-independent, so it works on any skeleton shape.

## Variants

- **Determinate**: ring, bar and gradient bar for a known fraction. `DSStepProgress` for a wizard or onboarding (4pt segments).
- **Counting**: `DSAnimatedNumber` with `.numericText` content transition for scores and totals.
- **Skeleton**: `.dsShimmer()` over placeholder shapes while content loads. `DSImageCard` uses it for its image placeholder.
- For indeterminate work with no fraction, use [DSThinkingIndicator](DSThinkingIndicator.md).

## Behavior

- The ring and both bars start at 0 and animate to `progress` on appear (`DSAnimation.progress`, 0.8s ease in-out), then animate again whenever `progress` changes. `DSAnimatedNumber` does the same with `DSAnimation.counting` (1s ease out).
- `DSStepProgress` does not start at 0: it draws `currentStep` filled segments at once and staggers the color change when `currentStep` changes, with `DSAnimation.stagger(index:)`.
- No haptics: these are status displays, not controls.
- `.dsShimmer()` does not start under Reduce Motion: the view simply stays static. The progress and counting animations are plain value transitions.

## Accessibility

- The progress views do not set an accessibility value of their own. Add one from outside so VoiceOver can report it, for example `.accessibilityLabel("Upload").accessibilityValue("\(Int(progress * 100)) percent")`.
- `DSAnimatedNumber` is text, so VoiceOver reads the number as it counts; it uses `.dsTextStyle(_:)` and scales with Dynamic Type.
- Shimmer placeholders are decorative; hide them with `.accessibilityHidden(true)` or label the container ("Loading").

## See also

- [DSThinkingIndicator](DSThinkingIndicator.md) for indeterminate work
- [Motion](Motion.md) for ambient effects
- [DSImageCard](DSCard.md) (shimmer placeholder)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSThinkingIndicator.md -->

# DSThinkingIndicator

An "the assistant is working" indicator: an animated SF Symbol next to a phrase that cycles and assembles letter by letter, for states where a spinner reads as frozen and a progress bar would be a lie.

![DSThinkingIndicator](../media/DSThinkingIndicator.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSThinkingIndicator.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSThinkingIndicator.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ThinkingDemo: View {
    @State private var isWorking = true

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                DSCard {
                    if isWorking {
                        DSThinkingIndicator(
                            phrases: ["Reading your notes", "Drafting a summary", "Almost there"]
                        )
                    } else {
                        Text("Summary ready").ds(.body)
                    }
                }
                .dsEdgeSweep(isActive: isWorking)

                DSButton(isWorking ? "Stop" : "Run again", variant: .secondary) {
                    isWorking.toggle()
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `phrases` | `[String]` | `["Thinking", "Weighing options", "Almost there"]` | Cycled in order, looping. A single phrase disables cycling but still assembles once on appear. |
| `symbol` | `String` | `"sparkles"` | SF Symbol for the leading animated glyph. |
| `interval` | `TimeInterval` | `2.6` | Seconds each phrase stays before the next one assembles. |
| `tint` | `Color?` | `nil` | Letter color. Defaults to `theme.ink`. The symbol always uses the theme gradient. |

## Variants

- **Default**: sparkles plus three phrases.
- **Custom copy**: pass your own phrases, for example `["Reading your notes", "Drafting a summary"]`.
- **Custom symbol**: any SF Symbol with layers, such as `"wand.and.stars"`.
- **With an edge sweep**: put it in a `DSCard` with `.dsEdgeSweep(isActive:)` as in the snippet, so the surface itself looks busy.

## Behavior

- The symbol uses the system's `.breathe.byLayer` and `.variableColor.iterative` effects, filled with the theme gradient.
- The phrase follows a wall-clock schedule, so it never desyncs when the view is re-created, and assembles letter by letter using `DSAnimation.stagger(index:)`.
- The row reserves the width of the widest phrase, so nothing around it shifts.
- No haptics: it is a status indicator, not an interaction.
- Reduce Motion: the symbol effects turn off and letters stop staggering, but phrases keep cycling as a plain cross-fade, because the phrase is information, not decoration.

## Accessibility

- The row is one element whose label is the whole current phrase, never a half-assembled fragment. The symbol is hidden from VoiceOver.
- It carries the `.updatesFrequently` trait, so VoiceOver does not interrupt the user with every change.
- Override from outside with `.accessibilityLabel("Generating summary")` if the phrases are too playful.
- Text uses `.dsTextStyle(.footnote)` and scales with Dynamic Type.

## See also

- [Progress](Progress.md) for known fractions
- [DSTypewriterText](DSTypewriterText.md)
- [Motion](Motion.md) (`.dsEdgeSweep`)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSSkeleton.md -->

# DSSkeleton

Loading placeholders: a shimmering block you compose by hand, and a `.dsSkeleton(_:)` modifier that turns a real view into its own placeholder so the loading layout can't drift from the loaded one.

![DSSkeleton](../media/DSSkeleton.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSSkeleton.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSSkeleton.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct SkeletonDemo: View {
    @State private var isLoading = true

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                // Hand-built placeholder
                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                    DSSkeleton.circle(DSSpacing.huge)
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                        DSSkeleton(width: 140)
                        DSSkeleton(width: 90)
                    }
                }

                // The real view, shown as its own placeholder while loading
                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                    DSAvatar(name: "Ada Lovelace", size: DSSpacing.huge)
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xxs) {
                        Text("Ada Lovelace").ds(.title3)
                        Text("Analyst, mathematician").ds(.callout)
                    }
                }
                .dsSkeleton(isLoading)

                DSToggle("Loading", isOn: $isLoading)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

`DSSkeleton(width:height:cornerRadius:)`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | `CGFloat?` | `nil` | Fixed width. `nil` fills the available width. |
| `height` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.sm` | Block height. |
| `cornerRadius` | `CGFloat` | `DSRadius.xs` | Corner radius. |

`DSSkeleton.circle(_ diameter:)` makes a round block, e.g. for an avatar.

`View.dsSkeleton(_ isLoading: Bool)` takes only the loading flag.

## Variants

```swift
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
    DSSkeleton(height: 160, cornerRadius: DSRadius.surface)
    DSSkeleton(height: DSSpacing.md)
    DSSkeleton(width: 120)
}
```
A feed-style block: image, title line, short subtitle.

## Behavior

- `DSSkeleton` is a block in the wash colour (on a backdrop) or the palette border colour (elsewhere), with a shimmer sweep.
- `.dsSkeleton(true)` redacts the view as placeholder shapes of its own layout, pulses its opacity gently between full and half (a 3.6 s cycle sampled from a timeline, so it stops the moment loading ends), and blocks touches.
- When `isLoading` goes false the redaction lifts with a short fade.
- The wrapped view keeps its identity when the flag flips: its `@State`, `.task` and `.onAppear` are not reset or run twice. That is why the modifier pulses instead of sweeping: a sweep needs a second copy of the content.
- Reduce Motion: no shimmer and no pulse. Placeholders rest at full opacity.

## Accessibility

- `DSSkeleton` blocks are hidden from VoiceOver.
- While `.dsSkeleton(true)` is active the view reads as one element labelled "Loading". When it ends, the real content is announced normally.

## See also

- [DSEmptyState](DSEmptyState.md)
- [DSCard](DSCard.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSSuccessCheck.md -->

# DSSuccessCheck

An animated success seal: the ring strokes itself, the disc fills, the checkmark draws, and the whole thing pops once with a soft halo and a success haptic on the same beat.

![DSSuccessCheck](../media/DSSuccessCheck.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSSuccessCheck.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSSuccessCheck.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct SuccessCheckDemo: View {
    @State private var isPaid = false

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                DSSuccessCheck(isComplete: isPaid, size: 96, accessibilityLabel: "Payment sent")
                    .padding(DSSpacing.md)
                Text(isPaid ? "Payment sent" : "Ready to pay").ds(.title2)
                DSButton(isPaid ? "Reset" : "Pay $24.00", isFullWidth: true) {
                    isPaid.toggle()
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isComplete` | `Bool` | required | Plays the animation when it becomes `true`. Fades the seal out when `false`. |
| `size` | `CGFloat` | `64` | Diameter of the seal. |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Ring and disc fill. Defaults to the theme's success color. The checkmark uses the palette's text-on-primary color. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle?` | `.success` | Fired as the check completes. `nil` for none. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `String` | `"Done"` | What VoiceOver says, and announces when the seal completes. |

## Variants

```swift
HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
    DSSuccessCheck(isComplete: true, size: 32)
    DSSuccessCheck(isComplete: true, size: 48, color: DSColors.info, haptic: nil)
}
```
The seal is only a fill and two strokes, so it works at any size from a list row up to a hero.

## Behavior

- The animation plays when `isComplete` becomes `true`, and once on first appear if it already is. A view that re-appears already complete (tab switch, navigating back) shows the finished seal at rest, with no haptic or announcement. It takes about 0.9 seconds.
- Order: the ring strokes itself, the disc fills behind it, then the check draws. A single spring pop peaks as the check finishes, together with one soft halo that expands and fades.
- The haptic fires at that peak, not at the start.
- When `isComplete` goes back to `false` the seal fades out quietly. Setting it to `true` again replays the animation.
- The halo extends past `size`; leave a little room around the seal.
- Reduce Motion: no strokes and no pop. The finished seal crossfades in, and the haptic still fires.

## Accessibility

- While complete, the seal is one image element labelled with your `accessibilityLabel`. While not complete it is hidden from VoiceOver.
- When it completes, the label is announced.
- Give it a label that says what happened ("Payment sent") rather than the default.

## See also

- [Progress](Progress.md) for work that is still running
- [Motion](Motion.md) for ambient effects
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSTypewriterText.md -->

# DSTypewriterText

Text that types a phrase out character by character, holds it, erases it and moves on to the next, with a blinking caret. For hero headlines and empty states that need a little life.

![DSTypewriterText](../media/DSTypewriterText.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSTypewriterText.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSTypewriterText.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct TypewriterDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                Text("Build something").ds(.largeTitle)
                DSTypewriterText(
                    ["that feels alive.", "with glass and springs.", "in an afternoon."],
                    style: .title1
                )

                DSTypewriterText(["Ready when you are."], style: .callout, loops: false)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

Keep phrases short enough to fit on one line: the view is single line and reserves the width of the widest phrase.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_ phrases` | `[String]` | required | Phrases to cycle through, in order. An empty array renders nothing. |
| `style` | `DSTextStyle` | `.title1` | Text style for the phrases. |
| `typingSpeed` | `TimeInterval` | `0.06` | Seconds per character while typing. |
| `erasingSpeed` | `TimeInterval` | `0.03` | Seconds per character while erasing. Should be faster than typing. |
| `holdDuration` | `TimeInterval` | `1.4` | Seconds a fully typed phrase stays before erasing. |
| `loops` | `Bool` | `true` | When `false`, stops on the last phrase fully typed (the caret keeps blinking). |
| `caretColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Caret fill. Defaults to the theme accent. |

## Variants

- **Rotating headline**: several phrases with `loops: true`.
- **Type once**: `loops: false` types the last phrase and stays (the snippet's second view).
- **Speed**: raise `typingSpeed` for a calmer feel; the defaults are about 16 characters per second.

## Behavior

- Steps through grapheme clusters, so emoji and accented characters are never split.
- Driven by a cancellable `Task`: cancelled on disappear and restarted when `phrases` or Reduce Motion changes.
- The caret blinks in `caretColor`; it is a thin capsule sized to the text style.
- No haptics.
- Reduce Motion: no typing or erasing; the full phrase is shown, still cycling through the list, and the caret stays solid.

## Accessibility

- The view is one element labelled with the whole current phrase, so VoiceOver never reads a half-typed fragment. The caret is decorative.
- Because the label changes when the phrase changes, avoid putting it where VoiceOver users need stable text, such as the only copy of an instruction.
- The text style applied through `.ds(_:)` scales with Dynamic Type. Check that your widest phrase still fits on one line at large sizes.

## See also

- [DSThinkingIndicator](DSThinkingIndicator.md)
- [DSEmptyState](DSEmptyState.md)
- [Motion](Motion.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/Motion.md -->

# Motion

Five composable view modifiers for ambient motion: breathe, jiggle, pop in, edge sweep and hue drift. Springs for touch, eased curves for ambience, and every one has a real Reduce Motion state.

![Motion](../media/Motion.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSMotion.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Animation/DSMotion.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct MotionDemo: View {
    @State private var shakes = 0
    @State private var isSweeping = true

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                Circle()
                    .fill(Color.green)
                    .frame(width: 16, height: 16)
                    .dsBreathe(.subtle)

                Image(systemName: "bell.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .dsJiggle(trigger: shakes)
                DSButton("Shake", variant: .secondary, size: .small) { shakes += 1 }

                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                    ForEach(0..<4, id: \.self) { index in
                        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: DSRadius.control, style: .continuous)
                            .fill(Color.blue)
                            .frame(height: DSSpacing.huge)
                            .dsHueDrift()
                            .dsPopIn(delay: Double(index) * 0.08)
                    }
                }

                Text("Processing…")
                    .ds(.body)
                    .padding(DSSpacing.md)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                    .dsSurface(.glass, radius: DSRadius.card)
                    .dsEdgeSweep(radius: DSRadius.card, isActive: isSweeping)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

### `.dsBreathe(_:)`

`func dsBreathe(_ intensity: DSBreatheIntensity = .medium) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_ intensity` | `DSBreatheIntensity` | `.medium` | How far it swells: `.subtle` (1.02), `.medium` (1.05), `.strong` (1.10). |

### `.dsJiggle(trigger:)`

`func dsJiggle<T: Equatable>(trigger: T) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `T: Equatable` | required | One decaying wiggle fires every time this value changes. |

### `.dsPopIn(delay:)`

`func dsPopIn(delay: Double = 0) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `delay` | `Double` | `0` | Seconds before the entrance starts. Stagger by index: `Double(index) * 0.08`. |

### `.dsEdgeSweep(radius:isActive:)`

`func dsEdgeSweep(radius: CGFloat = DSRadius.card, isActive: Bool = true) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `CGFloat` | `DSRadius.card` | Corner radius of the surface underneath. Match it. |
| `isActive` | `Bool` | `true` | Fades the highlight in and out. |

### `.dsHueDrift(isActive:)`

`func dsHueDrift(isActive: Bool = true) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isActive` | `Bool` | `true` | Turns the drift on or off. |

### `DSMotion.loop(_:autoreverses:unless:)`

For your own ambient effects: `DSMotion.loop(_ base: Animation, autoreverses: Bool = true, unless reduceMotion: Bool) -> Animation?` wraps an animation in `repeatForever`, or returns `nil` under Reduce Motion, so the change applies instantly and the effect rests instead of being skipped.

## Variants

| Modifier | Use it for | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| `.dsBreathe` | "alive and waiting": loading states, status dots, avatars | 2.4s ease-in-out loop, scale plus a slight opacity dip |
| `.dsJiggle` | a rejected input, an item that needs noticing | 0.45s, peak 7 degrees, decaying counter-swings |
| `.dsPopIn` | entrances and staggered rows | `springBouncy` overshoot from 0.8 scale |
| `.dsEdgeSweep` | processing, recording, "AI is working" | 2.0s linear loop of a specular highlight on the 1pt glass edge |
| `.dsHueDrift` | decorative life on a static gradient | 8.0s loop, at most 12 degrees of hue rotation |

The constants live on `DSMotion` (`breatheDuration`, `sweepDuration`, `driftDuration`, `driftDegrees`, `jiggleDegrees`, `jiggleDuration`).

`.dsPulse()` is deprecated; use `.dsBreathe(_:)` instead.

## Behavior

- All five settle at a resting state under Reduce Motion instead of being skipped: breathe and drift stop looping, the jiggle does not rotate, the edge sweep shows its highlight without travelling, and pop in keeps the fade but drops the scale.
- Colors come from the theme (the edge sweep is light riding the existing glass edge, not a border).
- The loops are ambient, so they do not fire haptics; add a `DSHapticEngine.shared.fire(.error)` next to a jiggle if the event deserves one.

## Accessibility

- These modifiers are purely visual and do not change what VoiceOver reads.
- Because Reduce Motion is a real state, content stays visible and in place when the setting is on.
- Never use motion as the only signal: pair a jiggle with an error message, and a sweep with a status text such as "Processing…".

## See also

- [DSThinkingIndicator](DSThinkingIndicator.md)
- [Progress](Progress.md)
- [DSAvatar](DSAvatar.md) (breathe while waiting)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSConfetti.md -->

# dsConfetti

A one-shot burst of confetti from any point of a view, fired whenever a trigger value changes. Colored from the active theme.

![dsConfetti](../media/DSConfetti.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSConfetti.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Animation/DSConfetti.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ConfettiDemo: View {
    @State private var celebrations = 0

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                Text("Order placed").ds(.title2)
                DSButton("Celebrate") { celebrations += 1 }
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
            .dsConfetti(trigger: celebrations, origin: UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.6))
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `Equatable` | required | One burst fires every time this value changes. It does not fire on first appearance. |
| `origin` | `UnitPoint` | `.center` | Where the burst starts, in the unit space of the view you attach it to. |
| `count` | `Int` | `80` | Number of pieces, limited to 150. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle?` | `nil` | Haptic fired with the burst. |

## Variants

```swift
struct ConfettiCornersDemo: View {
    @State private var left = 0
    @State private var right = 0

    var body: some View {
        VStack {
            DSButton("Both corners") { left += 1; right += 1 }
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .dsConfetti(trigger: left, origin: .bottomLeading, count: 50)
        .dsConfetti(trigger: right, origin: .bottomTrailing, count: 50, haptic: .success)
    }
}
```

Attach it to a container that covers the area the paper should fall through, such as the screen root, and pick `origin` in that container's unit space. Pieces are drawn inside the bounds of the view the modifier is attached to.

## Behavior

- Pieces fan upward and outward, slow down from air drag, then drift down under gravity while spinning and tumbling.
- Each piece lives 1.6 to 2.4 s and fades out over the last 30%.
- Colors come from the theme: the accent, the gradient stops, lighter tints of each, and the theme ink, which keeps the burst visible against the backdrop.
- Several triggers in a row overlap; earlier pieces finish their fall.
- Nothing runs while idle: the animation stops once the last piece is gone.
- `haptic` is `nil` by default because the action that triggers confetti (a button press, a confirmed slide) usually has its own haptic. Set it when the trigger is a state change with no haptic of its own.
- Reduce Motion: no pieces are drawn. The haptic, if set, still fires.

## Accessibility

- Purely decorative: ignores touches and is hidden from VoiceOver.
- Announce the outcome in your own UI (the success text or a toast), not through the confetti.

## See also

- [DSSlideToConfirm](DSSlideToConfirm.md)
- [DSToast](DSToast.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSMarquee.md -->

# DSMarquee

Content that scrolls horizontally in a seamless loop — but only when it is too wide to fit. A "now playing" line, a long title, a ticker of stats: text that would otherwise truncate keeps moving so all of it can be read. Content that already fits stays put.

![DSMarquee](../media/DSMarquee.gif)

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSMarquee.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSMarquee.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct NowPlaying: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                Text("Now playing").ds(.overline, color: DSColors.textSecondary)

                DSMarquee {
                    Text("Midnight City · M83 · Hurry Up, We're Dreaming").ds(.callout)
                }

                // Any content, not just text — it scrolls as one line.
                DSMarquee(velocity: 28) {
                    HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                        DSBadge("LIVE", variant: .filled)
                        Text("Breaking news scrolls by, in full").ds(.footnote)
                    }
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

Keep the content to a single line (text, a badge, a small row). The marquee measures that line and scrolls it only when it is wider than the space it has.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `velocity` | `CGFloat` | `40` | Scroll speed in points per second. Linear, so the pace reads constant for any length. `0` disables scrolling. |
| `spacing` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xxxl` (40) | Gap between the end of one copy and the start of the next in the loop. |
| `fade` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.lg` (20) | Width of the soft edge fade on each side. Pass `0` for hard edges. |
| `content` | `() -> Content` | required | The content to scroll, as a trailing `@ViewBuilder` closure. |

## Behavior

- **Scrolls only on overflow.** If the content fits the available width it is shown static and left-aligned, with no motion and no fade.
- **Seamless loop.** Two copies of the content are laid end to end with `spacing` between them, translated left by exactly one copy's width plus the gap, then wrapped — so the join never shows.
- **Edge fades.** A gradient mask (not a border) softens both edges while scrolling, hinting that the line continues past them. A static overflow fades only the trailing edge.
- **No haptics.** The marquee is ambient, not interactive.
- **Reduce Motion:** no scrolling. The content is shown static from its start with a trailing fade, so it is clearly truncated rather than frozen mid-scroll.

## Accessibility

- The content is exposed as a single combined element, so VoiceOver reads the whole line at once regardless of where the scroll happens to be. The second, looping copy and the hidden measuring copy are excluded from accessibility.
- Text styled with `.ds(_:)` scales with Dynamic Type; the line simply grows wider and scrolls further.
- Prefer a marquee for supplementary, glanceable copy (a track title, a status line). Don't put text a user must act on only inside a moving line.

## See also

- [DSTypewriterText](DSTypewriterText.md)
- [DSNumberTicker](DSNumberTicker.md)
- [Motion](Motion.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

# Onboarding

A four-page onboarding: welcome, theme picker, notification preferences and a celebratory finish.

> Example — not a component. Copy it and adapt it.

![Onboarding flow](../media/OnboardingFlow.png)

**Source:** [`OnboardingFlow.swift`](../../Examples/VelvetGallery/VelvetGallery/Flows/OnboardingFlow.swift)

## What it demonstrates

- [DSButton](../components/DSButton.md): one full-width button that reads "Continue", then "Get started" on the last page.
- [DSPageControl](../components/DSPageControl.md): dots that follow the swipe and jump on tap.
- [DSTypewriterText](../components/DSTypewriterText.md): the welcome headline cycling through short phrases.
- [DSCard](../components/DSCard.md), [DSToggle](../components/DSToggle.md) and [DSSegmentedControl](../components/DSSegmentedControl.md): the preferences page.
- [DSSuccessCheck](../components/DSSuccessCheck.md) and [DSConfetti](../components/DSConfetti.md): the finish.
- Motion modifiers: `.dsBreathe(.subtle)` on the glyph and `.dsPopIn(delay:)` for staggered entrances ([Motion](../components/Motion.md)).

## How it works

- The flow owns a `DSTheme` in `@State` and injects it with `.dsTheme(theme)` at its root. The theme page sets `theme.gradient` inside `withAnimation(DSAnimation.normal)`, so the backdrop crossfades.
- Pages are a paging `TabView` on iOS. On macOS the flow shows the current page only.
- Each page builds its content only while it is the current page, so the pop-in stagger replays every visit.
- Arriving on the last page flips `DSSuccessCheck(isComplete:)` and bumps the confetti trigger on the same beat. The confetti is attached to the full-screen container, because it draws inside the view it is attached to.
- `onFinish` runs when you press "Get started".

## Run it

Gallery → Examples → Onboarding.

## Copy it

```bash
swift velvet.swift add Onboarding --dest MyApp/VelvetUI
```

<!-- source: docs/examples/Settings.md -->

# Settings

A settings screen with a profile header, preference toggles, a theme detail screen and a slide-to-confirm account deletion.

> Example — not a component. Copy it and adapt it.

![Settings flow](../media/SettingsFlow.png)

**Source:** [`SettingsFlow.swift`](../../Examples/VelvetGallery/VelvetGallery/Flows/SettingsFlow.swift)

## What it demonstrates

- [DSCard](../components/DSCard.md), [DSAvatar](../components/DSAvatar.md) and [DSBadge](../components/DSBadge.md): the profile header.
- [DSListCell](../components/DSListCell.md) with `DSDivider` and `DSSectionHeader`: grouped rows inside `DSCard(padding: 0)`.
- [DSToggle](../components/DSToggle.md) and [DSSegmentedControl](../components/DSSegmentedControl.md): preferences.
- [DSSheet](../components/DSSheet.md) and [DSSlideToConfirm](../components/DSSlideToConfirm.md): the delete-account confirmation, tinted with the error color.
- [DSToast](../components/DSToast.md): "Saved" feedback.

## How it works

- `SettingsFlow` has no `NavigationStack` of its own, because nested stacks are unsupported. The host provides one (the Gallery pushes it inside its list's stack); wrap it in `NavigationStack { SettingsFlow() }` to show it standalone.
- Appearance (System, Light, Dark) really drives `.preferredColorScheme` on the flow.
- The Theme row pushes a detail screen. Choosing a theme sets `theme.gradient` in `withAnimation`, so the backdrop crossfades behind the navigation bar.
- Changing any toggle, the appearance or the theme shows a "Saved" toast for about 1.6 s. There is one toast at a time: a new one replaces the old and restarts the timer.
- "Delete account" opens a sheet. The slide awaits a fake service, shows "Deleted", then the sheet closes and a toast confirms.
- Email and Password rows are navigation rows that show an info toast, to keep the example short.

## Run it

Gallery → Examples → Settings.

## Copy it

```bash
swift velvet.swift add Settings --dest MyApp/VelvetUI
```

<!-- source: docs/examples/Checkout.md -->

# Checkout

A cart with quantity steppers, a promo code, a rolling total and a slide to pay that ends in a confirmation.

> Example — not a component. Copy it and adapt it.

![Checkout flow](../media/CheckoutFlow.png)

**Source:** [`CheckoutFlow.swift`](../../Examples/VelvetGallery/VelvetGallery/Flows/CheckoutFlow.swift)

## What it demonstrates

- [DSCard](../components/DSCard.md) and [DSStepper](../components/DSStepper.md): line items, each stepper labelled with the item name for VoiceOver.
- [DSTextField](../components/DSTextField.md) and [DSButton](../components/DSButton.md): the promo code with success and error states.
- [DSNumberTicker](../components/DSNumberTicker.md): the total rolls whenever a quantity or the promo changes.
- [DSSlideToConfirm](../components/DSSlideToConfirm.md): pay, with `finish: .morphAndVanish` handing off to the success state.
- [DSSuccessCheck](../components/DSSuccessCheck.md) and [DSConfetti](../components/DSConfetti.md): the confirmation.
- [DSEmptyState](../components/DSEmptyState.md): the empty cart.

## How it works

- Try the code `VELVET` for 10% off. Any other code shows the error state. Editing the code clears the result.
- The slide's `onConfirm` awaits `CheckoutService.charge` (about 1.2 s). Turn on "Simulate a declined card" to make it throw: the control re-opens and a message explains why. While the charge runs the cart steppers, promo field and decline toggle are disabled, so the charged total is the one shown.
- On success the slide plays its `.morphAndVanish` finish; about 0.9 s later (in a cancellable `Task`) the view swaps to the confirmation with `DSAnimation.springSmooth`, and the confetti trigger is bumped on the same beat. The confirmation's `DSSuccessCheck` passes `haptic: nil`, so the payment has a single success haptic (the slide's). The confetti is attached to the root container, which covers the screen.
- "Done" calls `onFinish()`, resets the cart, and remounts the slide with a new `.id` so it starts fresh.
- Set every quantity to 0 to see the empty state with "Restore cart". The pay control is hidden while the cart is empty.

## Run it

Gallery → Examples → Checkout.

## Copy it

